title: Burns Anaesthesia Fellowship
inst: Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre
Department: Department of Anesthesia, Sunnybrook / University of Toronto Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine
Duration: 12 months (shorter or longer may be pursued under certain circumstances)
Deadline: Apply at least 15 months in advance; January 2027 session closed; online forms open for July 2027 and January 2028 intakes
Eligibility: Minimum 30 months of clinical anaesthesia training and all requisite certification exams passed in home country; preference for training completed within past seven years; fluency in English mandatory
International applicants: Yes — open to international graduates; applicants whose first language is not English must pass TOEFL/TSE or IELTS
Accreditation: University of Toronto PGME-registered fellowship; does not count towards Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada specialty certification
Application method: Online application form via University of Toronto Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine website (one intake period per application) with letter of intent and signed reference letters
Funding: Institution policy: clinical fellows must be funded (department or sponsoring agency); FEAC recommends pay at least equal to PGY1 on the PARO salary scale, and foreign nationals must be paid at a rate commensurate with a Canadian in the same role
Visa support: Institution policy: international clinical fellows need an IRCC work permit; the PGME Office issues an LMIA-exempt offer of employment number and supports the work permit application
Licence requirement: Temporary CPSO licence on acceptance, then educational licence after a mandated 1–3 month assessment period; fellow must procure malpractice insurance
Summary: A one-year fellowship focused on perioperative anaesthetic management and ICU care of patients with burn injuries at the Ross Tilley Burn Centre, the largest burn care centre in Canada.

Department: University of Toronto Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine
Deadline: Apply ~18 months ahead; applications close 9 months before start (e.g. July 2027 closed 30 Sept 2026; February 2028 closes 1 Feb 2027; August 2028 closes 1 Aug 2027)
Eligibility: Anaesthesiologists, physiatrists and gynaecologists interested in comprehensive pain management in women's health
International applicants: Yes — University of Toronto fellowships accept international graduates; English proficiency required where training was not in English
Accreditation: University of Toronto PGME-registered fellowship; does not count towards Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada specialty certification
Application method: Online application platform on the University of Toronto Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine website
Funding: Institution policy: Fellowships funded by department, sponsoring agency or external source; PGME guidelines recommend at least PARO PGY1-equivalent remuneration and pay commensurate with a Canadian in the same role for visa trainees
Visa support: Institution policy: Foreign nationals need an LMIA-exempt work permit; U of T PGME issues the IRCC offer-of-employment number and CPSO letter of eligibility about 5 months before start
Licence requirement: Eligibility for registration with University of Toronto PGME and a postgraduate education certificate of registration from the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario
Summary: A twelve-month fellowship in comprehensive, evidence-based pain management within women's health, combining interventional pain techniques with interdisciplinary integrated care.

International applicants: Yes - the Honorary Clinical Fellowship scheme offers foreign doctors attachments to NUH specialties

Visa support: Training Employment Pass (TEP) from Ministry of Manpower required; dependants' passes cannot be applied for under the TEP
Licence requirement: Temporary Medical Registration with the Singapore Medical Council
Summary: Honorary clinical fellowship in hand and reconstructive microsurgery, with an advanced fellowship option.

Deadline: 1 August of the year preceding the start date (ERAS)
Eligibility: Successful completion of three years of postgraduate training in an accredited internal medicine residency
International applicants: Institution policy: Graduates of non-US medical schools eligible if ECFMG-certified before appointment (applicants still obtaining certification may interview but cannot be ranked or appointed) or holding a full unrestricted licence in the programme state; Canadian graduates after 1 July 2025 also need ECFMG certification

Deadline: Even semester 2026/2027: online registration 1 September - 3 November 2026 (19:00 WIB); TPA and English test 7 November 2026 on Campus C. Odd semester 2026/2027 registration ran 1 April - 22 June 2026
Eligibility: Indonesian specialist in dermatology, venereology and aesthetics (Sp.DVE) (domestic or foreign graduate; foreign-trained specialists need an adaptation certificate from a collegium-recognised institution); legalised specialist diploma; valid specialist STR; collegium recommendation; employer consent if employed; signed statement to comply with RSUD Dr. Soetomo/FK UNAIR rules; family consent. Sp.DVE diploma and transcript; ELPT/TOEFL >= 500; evidence of interest; mental-health test package at RSUD Dr. Soetomo psychiatry department; priority to applicants from DVE education institutions or tertiary-care hospitals.
International applicants: Indonesian citizens only (Warga Negara Indonesia); Indonesian specialists who trained abroad are eligible with an adaptation certificate
Application method: Online registration via PPMB Universitas Airlangga (ppmb.unair.ac.id), selection fee, TPA and English test, then programme subject exam, health test/MMPI and interview; hard-copy documents for stage-1 passers
Funding: Self-funded or sponsored; fees 2026/2027: UKT Rp 25,000,000 per semester plus one-off IPI Rp 40,000,000. Ministry of Health study-assignment candidates need a letter confirming MoH/health office covers UKT and IPI
Visa support: Not applicable (Indonesian citizens only)
Licence requirement: Valid Indonesian specialist STR (at least 6 months before expiry); RSUD Dr. Soetomo practice permit (SIP) during training where stated
Summary: FK UNAIR's dermatology subspecialist (Sp2) programme currently admits Indonesian dermatologists to its tropical dermatology interest.

Department: Division of Rheumatology
Start: Institution policy: University of Toronto PGME academic year runs 1 July - 30 June (letters of appointment issued per academic year; off-cycle starts possible)
Eligibility: Institution policy: must be eligible for a CPSO postgraduate education certificate, including recognition as a medical specialist/family physician in the jurisdiction where the applicant practised before the fellowship
International applicants: Institution policy: Yes - international applicants who meet CPSO clinical-fellow licensure requirements contact the Fellowship Program Director; applicants from countries with training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency to the PGME Office
Accreditation: Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada accredited
Application method: Email rheumatology.trainingprogram@sickkids.ca
Funding: Institution policy: clinical fellows must be funded (department or sponsoring agency); FEAC recommends pay at least equal to PGY1 on the PARO salary scale, and foreign nationals must be paid at a rate commensurate with a Canadian in the same role
Visa support: Institution policy: international clinical fellows need an IRCC work permit; the PGME Office issues an LMIA-exempt offer of employment number and supports the work permit application
Licence requirement: Institution policy: clinical fellows must hold a CPSO certificate of registration authorising postgraduate education (educational licence); research fellows do not need CPSO registration
Summary: Two-year paediatric rheumatology training with specialised lupus, vasculitis and dermatomyositis clinics, an adult rheumatology rotation and a scholarly project.

title: International Paediatric Sponsorship Scheme (IPSS)
inst: Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH)
Department: International Office
Start: Flexible (proposed start at least four months ahead)
Eligibility: Job offer for an NHS post with a strong training/educational component (usually ST3–ST8 equivalent); GMC-accepted PMQ (ECFMG verified); 3-year postgraduate paediatric qualification accepted by RCPCH; 36 of last 60 and 10 of last 12 months clinical practice; no failed PLAB in last 3 years
International applicants: After the NHS England pause of MTI, IPSS is now open to all doctors outside the EEA (page updated 28 August 2026); IELTS Academic 7.0 each/7.5 overall or OET Medicine B
Application method: Screening by RCPCH (job description, post submission form, CV, English scores) then sponsorship application; contact ipss@rcpch.ac.uk
Funding: No application fee; must enrol as RCPCH Associate Member
Visa support: IPSS cannot help with visas; the employer usually provides a Skilled Worker visa
Licence requirement: RCPCH sponsorship route to GMC registration
Summary: RCPCH sponsorship route to GMC registration for international paediatricians who have secured an NHS training-focused post.

Department: Division of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery
Start: Institution policy: Preferred start 1 July; otherwise must start on the first of a month
Deadline: 1 February of the year prior to beginning the fellowship
Eligibility: Completion of OTL-HNS, General Surgery or General Plastic Surgery residency; interview with director
International applicants: Open to international candidates with fellowship/board certification (or national equivalent); foreign graduates must obtain a Canadian training visa and an Alberta educational licence
Accreditation: American Head and Neck Society and Canadian Association of Head and Neck Surgical Oncologists
Application method: Institution policy: Apply directly to the fellowship programme per its guidelines; offers subject to PGME approval (sponsored applicants from Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, UAE apply via sponsor to PGME)
Funding: Institution policy: Fellowships without salary/funding not permitted; from 1 Jan 2026 salary must be at least the PARA R1 level; PGME provides no salary
Visa support: Institution policy: International fellows require a Canadian work permit before starting; PGME issues the offer/FVCA number, documents due to PGME at least 6 months before start
Licence requirement: Institution policy: College of Physicians & Surgeons of Alberta (CPSA) registration required before clinical fellowship begins, incl. CPSA English language proficiency where applicable
Summary: A one-year fellowship accredited by the AHNS and CAHNSO, with a minimum of 150 microvascular reconstructions and 30-40 TORS procedures.

title: G. Raymond Chang Forensic Pathology Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – Laboratory Medicine and Pathobiology / Ontario Forensic Pathology Service

Licence requirement: CPSO educational licence (postgraduate certificate of registration) required; CMPA malpractice coverage
Summary: Clinical fellowship in amputee management from pre-amputation consults to inpatient and outpatient prosthetic rehabilitation at Sunnybrook and UHN-West Park, including traumatic and burns-related amputations.
